body.statement: For any \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies equality of their skeletons and \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\in V\). More precisely, the inclusion-minimal nonempty supports in \(T_C^{\circ}\) are exactly \(\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}\) for \(B\in\Pi_j\); every support of size at least two has a unique center \(j\) and recovers the labelled block \(B\), while a support of size one recovers only the underlying edge. Thus every edge whose orientation differs between \(G\) and \(H\) is a singleton block in both states.
body.justification: The tangent support partition is the first orientation-robust observable that distinguishes repeated incoming coefficient blocks from reversible singleton edges.
body.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 4.1 and Section 5, gives smoothness and fixed-graph rational recovery but no cross-DAG recovery of target-local blocks from equality of model images.
body.consumer: The lemma lets a covariance-model comparison recover causal communities without knowing which Markov-equivalent orientation generated them.
